html:
SMTO-WEB-0023 — SMTO couldn't match the answer's sources to a page it actually read

GUID: 7dc027a6-2680-5634-b047-5b77f0b2c961
Slug: research-evidence-receipt-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a record of every page it reads. The sources in this answer don't line up with a finished, unchanged record, so SMTO won't present them as proven.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to rebuild that part from pages it has fully read. The check failed because a reading was incomplete, out of date or didn't match what was stored.
  2. If the run stops, ask SMTO to read the source page again and then answer. A fresh, complete reading gives the answer a record that matches exactly.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. The answer is then shown even though part of it can't be traced to a complete reading.

What success looks like

  • The answer appears with links to the pages it relied on.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details name the reading that didn't match. Don't treat a missing, unfinished or outdated reading as if it succeeded.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof could not resolve a complete, successful, non-stale operation receipt matching the source's operation ID, capability and content digest, or the span locator did not resolve inside that receipt.

What this means

  • Proof cannot resolve a complete successful receipt matching the source's operation, capability and content digest, or the span locator cannot resolve within it. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • Proof cannot resolve a complete successful receipt matching the source's operation, capability and content digest, or the span locator cannot resolve within it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect receipt status, scope, digest, staleness and locator without creating substitute receipts.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_evidence_receipt_invalid by _verify_source or _verify_fact: resolve_evidence failed, the receipt was incomplete, unsuccessful, stale, had a different capability_id or content digest, or located(receipt.data, span.locator) failed. Inspect the run's receipts for the operation ID in the rejection details; re-acquire the page through Web Read so the claim binds to a fresh valid receipt.
  • Restore valid retained receipt references or obtain fresh authorized evidence for the affected claim.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact source and span resolve against eligible current receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a missing, stale, or ineligible receipt as a successful observation.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
